ambiguities.source_text: Reduce the dataset down to a single row per Wildlife Species, with the minimum and maximum temperatures they live in in the wild
ambiguities.intent: Group by Wildlife and Name; use the minimum habitat lower bound and maximum habitat upper bound across all listed habitats, in one chosen temperature unit.

ambiguities.source_text: Reduce the San Diego Climate Table to a single row which describes the temperature range in San Diego
ambiguities.intent: Use the minimum low and maximum high across all climate months in the chosen unit.

ambiguities.source_text: you may choose to work in either Fahrenheit or Celsius
ambiguities.intent: Either Fahrenheit or Celsius is allowed. Use the corresponding supplied climate columns and habitat values consistently, and report all Degrees outside Ideal values in that same unit. The supplied F and C estimates are not always exact conversions; do not mix them.

ambiguities.source_text: Degrees outside Ideal - if the wildlife is not in their ideal temperature range, the signed number of degrees San Diego can be above or below the ideal temperature range
ambiguities.intent: Degrees outside Ideal is signed: sd_high minus wild_max for Above; sd_low minus wild_min for Below; zero for Ideal. Keep the signed deviation in the final output; only the ranking intermediate is absolute.
